citations.assessment: Entry 1881 and the Shabbat narrative name Yonatan ben Elazar alongside Akhmai or Akhinai.
The Bavli explicitly gives Yonatan ben Elazar in the discussion of purity and distinguishes Yonatan ben Amram immediately after him.
The reciprocal entry compares Yochanan in Bekhorot and Yonatan in Shabbat. The pointer resolves independently of the proposed identity.

holds.raw: היוחסין כתב ר' יוחנן בן אלעזר בזמן רבב"ח
holds.reason: Bekhorot establishes that bar bar Chana quotes Yochanan ben Elazar. The exact Yuchasin notice was not located in the checked chronological transcription.
The primary witnesses support both names and the Lakonya connection, without explicitly making the two names one person.

holds.raw: ר' שמואל ב"נ בשמו הוא ר' יונתן סתם
holds.reason: The checked teacher designation uses bare Yonatan. The specific attribution to ben Elazar remains held, preserving Heilprin’s objection.
